## Research Notes
Truth map: `research.md`. Decisions D1–D6 are in `spec.md`. Key findings:
- `record` applies each flag inside its argument loop and writes once at the end (`hooks/ledger.sh:687,709`).
  The signature flags may come before or after `--item-kind`, so the kind change has to be applied **after** the
  loop, once every flag has been read.
- `hooks/ledger.sh` is 961 lines, over the 500-line code limit. The commit gate warns when a file that is already
  over the limit grows. So the new logic goes in `hooks/ledger-automerge.sh` (334 lines). The guard exists for
  merge-auto, and its sibling `verified_head_set`, the launcher-only `record` flag, already lives there
  (`hooks/ledger-automerge.sh:38-55`). `ledger.sh` grows by only the argument parsing and one call.
- The ask rule, `is_person_sub` and lane-guard's plain-spelling check already handle `record … --reviewed-by-human`
  (`hooks/lane-lib.sh:56`, `hooks/lane-guard.sh:120`). The one thing missing is the ask rule itself
  (`hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:144`).
- `tests/smoke-automerge.sh` is about 485 lines of code (review round 1, measured with the gate's regex at
  `hooks/quality-before-commit.sh:210`). The new block would push it past 500, which the gate blocks. The new
  cases therefore go in a new part file, `tests/smoke-item-kind.sh`. It is sourced from `smoke-automerge.sh`
  right before that file's cleanup (`rm -rf "$am_t"`, its last lines), so it reuses the fixture (`am`,
  `am_entry`, `am_pr`, `am_case`, `am_no`, `am_grant`, `am_ld`, FakeGhPr). The cost is one line in
  `smoke-automerge.sh`. The new file creates its own branches (`ik1`…`ik4` from `dev`, pushed), because the
  fixture's `feat*` branches belong to earlier cases.
- The board item asks for the launcher path ("a person's signature … or the launcher's"). It has no caller today:
  only `init` and `record` write the kind, and `hooks/session-launch.sh:233,240` only reads it. It is kept so that
  a future launcher re-read of the board kind is never refused (review round 1, item 6).

## Data Model
The ledger entry gains `intake_kind` (string: `feature|incident|vulnerability`). `init` writes it, and only a
signed change or a launcher change rewrites it. Entries written before this change have no `intake_kind`, and
readers fall back to `item_kind`. A new event kind, `item-kind-changed`, is added to `.events[]`.

## API Contracts
New CLI form: `ledger.sh record <id> --item-kind <k> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>`. Without the signature or
the launcher marker, a change away from `incident`/`vulnerability` exits 1 and writes nothing. When
`--reviewed-by-human`/`--by` is given without `--item-kind`, the call exits 1. Exit codes of `automerge` are
unchanged.

## Implementation Approach
1. **Intake kind at `init`**: add `intake_kind: $ik` to the entry literal.
2. **Deferred kind change in `record`**: the loop collects `NEWKIND`, `REVIEWED` and `RBY`. After the loop,
   `item_kind_set` runs whenever `NEWKIND` or the signature was given. It checks, in this order:
   - the signature appears without `--item-kind` → refuse;
   - the value is valid (the existing message is kept);
   - the current kind is incident/vulnerability and the new kind is different → the change needs the launcher
     marker or a signature. A signature means **both** `--reviewed-by-human` and a `--by` that matches
     `AM_NAME_RE`, the same rule as `hooks/ledger-automerge.sh:170`. Either flag alone is refused, and so is a
     signature inside a worker;
   - when signed or made by the launcher, it sets both fields. If either `item_kind` or `intake_kind` changes
     (review round 1, item 4: a signed call that only rewrites `intake_kind` removes a gate too), it appends the
     `item-kind-changed` event. The note carries both fields, for example
     `item_kind incident → feature; intake_kind incident → feature`. When unsigned (an upgrade or the same kind),
     it sets `item_kind` only.
   Every refusal calls `die` before `write_entry`, so the file is left untouched (SC-002).
3. **Automerge reads both kinds**: the gate list becomes `[.item_kind, .intake_kind] | unique[]`, filtered to
   incident/vulnerability. A missing `intake_kind` is null and the filter drops it, so a legacy entry falls back
   to `item_kind` without a dead `//` branch.
4. **Ask rule**: one list entry. `tests/smoke-signatures.sh` reads the list, so its completeness and
   `is_person_sub` checks cover the new entry. The hand-written `sg_rows` table gets one row (Test Plan,
   FR-009).
5. **Smoke tests**: assertions sit at the tool-call level. "No merge" is checked as no `pr merge` line in the fake
   gh log (constitution 3). There are two mutations, each made with sed on a copy of `ledger-automerge.sh`, and
   each is first checked as applied (`cmp -s` against the original fails, as in `tests/smoke-signatures.sh:176,192`).
   - **M1, the guard line deleted** (the `case "$cur" in incident|vulnerability) … die …` line removed). It is
     caught by the unsigned-`record` case: the call now exits 0 and the entry file changes (`cmp`). The merge
     case does not catch M1, by design: `intake_kind` still gates the merge.
   - **M2, `intake_kind` dropped from automerge's jq program.** It is caught by the hand-edited case (item
     `feature`, intake `incident`): `gh pr merge` now appears in the fake gh log.
   - **M3, the session-id half of the launcher marker dropped** (`am_is_launcher` reduced to the
     `HEFESTO_LAUNCHER` test). It is caught by the FR-002 case that sets `HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1` together with
     `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`: the unsigned downgrade now exits 0 and the file changes.
   - **M4, the `REVIEWED` test dropped from `item_kind_signer`.** It is caught by the FR-004 case
     `record <id> --item-kind feature --by Ana` with no `--reviewed-by-human`: the call now exits 0 and the file
     changes.
   - **M5, `.item_kind` dropped from automerge's union** (leaving `[.intake_kind]`). It is caught by the FR-006
     case with item `incident` and intake `feature` (an unsigned upgrade): `gh pr merge` now appears in the log.
   **How a mutant runs.** `ledger.sh` finds its sourced files through `HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"`
   (`hooks/ledger.sh:71`). Each mutation therefore builds a temp hooks folder: every file in `hooks/` symlinked,
   `ledger.sh` copied (so `HERE` is the temp folder), and the mutated `ledger-automerge.sh` written as a real file
   in place of its link. The run goes through `AM_LG="$tmp/ledger.sh" am …` and `am_case …` (the `am` override
   above), so the gh-log assertion is the same one the plain cases use.
6. **One launcher test in `ledger-automerge.sh`.** A new `am_is_launcher()` holds
   `[ "${HEFESTO_LAUNCHER:-}" = 1 ] && [ -z "${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}" ]`. `verified_head_set` (`:46`) and
   `item_kind_set` both call it, so M3 mutates one place. `launcher_gate` in `ledger.sh:286` keeps its own copy;
   moving it is outside this item.
7. **Complexity.** `item_kind_set` is split so each function stays under complexity 10:
   `item_kind_signer` (prints `launcher`, the `--by` name, or nothing; dies on a worker or a malformed name) and
   `item_kind_set` (the value check, the guard, the write and the event).

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: `record` collects, then applies
**File:** `hooks/ledger.sh` (modify at `:685-709`)
**Intent:** the signature can come anywhere in the argument list; the kind is applied once, after the loop.

```bash
ID=…; E=…; NEWKIND=""; REVIEWED=0; RBY=""; HAVE_KIND=0; HAVE_SIG=0
  --item-kind) NEWKIND="${2:-}"; HAVE_KIND=1; shift ;;
  --reviewed-by-human) REVIEWED=1; HAVE_SIG=1 ;; --by) RBY="${2:-}"; HAVE_SIG=1; shift ;;
…; esac; shift; done
[ "$HAVE_KIND$HAVE_SIG" = 00 ] || item_kind_set "$HAVE_KIND" "$NEWKIND"   # ledger-automerge.sh; `--by ''` alone is refused too
write_entry "$ID" <<<"$E" || exit 1
```

**Why this shape:** `ledger.sh` stays as close to its current size as possible. A single call site means one
place to mutate.

### Sketch 2: the guard
**File:** `hooks/ledger-automerge.sh` (new, after `verified_head_set` `:55`)
**Intent:** a kind change away from incident/vulnerability is a person's signature or the launcher's own record.

```bash
item_kind_set() { # $1 1 when --item-kind was given, $2 the kind — reads REVIEWED, RBY; updates E
  local cur by=""
  [ "$1" = 1 ] || die "ledger record $ID: --reviewed-by-human / --by apply to --item-kind only (nothing would read the signature)"
  in_list "$2" "feature incident vulnerability" || die "ledger record $ID: --item-kind must be feature, incident or vulnerability (got '$2')"
  cur=$(jq -r '.item_kind // "feature"' <<<"$E")
  by=$(item_kind_signer) || exit 1   # launcher (am_is_launcher) | the --by name | ""; dies on a worker or a bad name
  # item_kind_signer: a signature is REVIEWED = 1 AND RBY =~ AM_NAME_RE (as ledger-automerge.sh:170) — never --by
  # alone: the ask rule, SIGN_FLAGS and is_person_sub key on --reviewed-by-human, so `--by` alone would get no dialog
  case "$cur" in incident|vulnerability) [ "$2" = "$cur" ] || [ -n "$by" ] || die "ledger record $ID: $cur → $2 drops the $cur gate — a person signs it: ledger.sh record $ID --item-kind $2 --reviewed-by-human --by <name>" ;; esac
  # signed/launcher → both fields + an item-kind-changed event when EITHER field changes; unsigned → item_kind only
}
```

**Why this shape:** it follows the same pattern as `verified_head_set` (marker test, worker refusal, name regex
`AM_NAME_RE`). Each refusal names the form that would succeed (exception messages carry the evidence).

### Sketch 3: automerge's gate list
**File:** `hooks/ledger-automerge.sh` (modify at `:239`)
**Intent:** the kind recorded at intake is always gated, whatever `item_kind` reads now.

```bash
for g in verify review quality scan $(jq -r '[.item_kind, .intake_kind] | unique[]
    | select(. == "incident" or . == "vulnerability")' <<<"$1"); do
```

**Why this shape:** D3 says the heavier kind wins. Legacy entries fall back to `item_kind`. The existing "gate X
is not PASS" message and the `human:merge` skip stay as they are.

### Sketch 4: the forged downgrade smoke case
**File:** `tests/smoke-item-kind.sh` (new; sourced from `tests/smoke-automerge.sh` before its cleanup; branches `ik1`…`ik4`)
**Intent:** forge both ways and assert on the gh log.

```bash
am_entry HEF-40 … '.item_kind = "incident" | .intake_kind = "incident"'
am_no "unsigned downgrade" "a person signs it" record HEF-40 --item-kind feature   # then: file byte-identical (cmp)
am_entry HEF-41 … '.item_kind = "feature" | .intake_kind = "incident"'; am_pr …
am_case "forged item_kind under an incident intake" HEF-41 2 human:merge "gate incident is not PASS"   # no gh pr merge
am_ok "signed downgrade" record HEF-42 --item-kind feature --reviewed-by-human --by Ana; am_case … HEF-42 0 none "merged"
```

**Why this shape:** it reuses `am_entry`, `am_case` and `am_no`. `am_case` already fails when `gh pr merge` was
invoked on a non-zero exit. The new branches keep the merge cases independent of the fixture's earlier ones.

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **Principle 1** (payload not under `.claude/`): only payload files at the repo root (`hooks/`, `tests/`,
  `docs/`) change.
- [x] **Principle 2** (namespaced commands): no command is added.
- [x] **Principle 3** (mutation-tested, tool-call assertions): five mutations are planned (M1 to M5), one for
  each guard half. The "no merge"
  assertion is on the fake gh invocation log.
- [x] **Principle 4** (zero-install): bash and jq only.
- [x] **Principle 5** (helpers fail loudly): every refusal exits 1 with the reason and the signed form. There is
  no sentinel.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| The fixture's `feat*` branches are used by earlier blocks, and a merged branch cannot be merged again | the new merge case fails for fixture reasons | `tests/smoke-item-kind.sh` creates and pushes its own `ik1`…`ik4` |
| `tests/smoke-automerge.sh` crosses 500 lines of code (it is about 485 today) | the commit gate blocks it | the cases live in `tests/smoke-item-kind.sh`; `smoke-automerge.sh` gains one line |
| The test is read as proof against an entry-file write | the CHANGELOG overclaims | `intake_kind` is a second layer behind the `record` guard: it catches a future unguarded writer, but not a session that can write the ledger file. That folder lives outside the sandbox's write set, which is its own defence. The CHANGELOG says this (review round 1, item 7) |
| An existing test downgrades without a signature | it goes red | the search found none; `tests/smoke.sh:3602` is an upgrade (feature → vulnerability) and stays green |
| `record --reviewed-by-human` under `auto` permission mode shows no dialog | a session could self-sign | same premise as every other signature (D6). `session-start-context.sh` already warns. Out of scope |
| A set-up project has no ask rule for the new flag until `hefesto-setup.sh` runs again (`record:*` is allowed) | the orchestrator signs with no dialog | `### Upgrade` line in the CHANGELOG. `hefesto-setup.sh --check` reports the rule missing, as it does for any missing signature rule |
| `init` pre-emption: a session runs `init <id> … --item-kind feature` before `register` | both kinds are fixed at `feature`, and the gate is lost | out of scope (spec D6). CHANGELOG known issue, proposed as a follow-up board item. Until then, keep `merge_by: lane` on boards that carry incident or vulnerability items, as 9.4.1 already advises |
| A legacy entry was downgraded before the fix | its incident gate is lost | the fallback is `item_kind`, so a past forgery is not detected. The CHANGELOG tells people to check incident/vulnerability entries recorded before 9.4.2 |
| `ledger.sh` grows past its HEAD size | commit-gate advisory | about 3 net lines; the logic lives in `ledger-automerge.sh` |

## Quick Start
1. Write `tests/smoke-item-kind.sh` (Sketch 4, every row of the Test Plan), its source line in
   `smoke-automerge.sh`, the `sg_rows` row, and the `tests/smoke.sh` assertions. Run them and confirm they are
   red.
2. `init` `intake_kind`, then `item_kind_set` and the `record` wiring, then the automerge union.
3. The setup list entry, the docs and the CHANGELOG. Then `bash tests/smoke.sh` and `shellcheck hooks/*.sh`.
